findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user who has never interacted with the topic has no topic_users row). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, which raises NoMethodError on nil and produces a 500 error. The unsubscribe link is sent in notification emails to any recipient, including users who never opened the topic, so this path is reachable in normal use. The code should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` (which creates the row if missing, as done in #set_notifications) or guard against nil.

findings.title: unsubscribe action does not verify the user can see the topic
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe builds `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` but never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!` on the topic. TopicView.new may raise Discourse::InvalidAccess for restricted topics, but for topics the user cannot see the action still mutates TopicUser state and renders the show response via perform_show_response, leaking topic existence/content (title, excerpt via @description_meta) to users without access. Compare with #show, which rescues Discourse::InvalidAccess, and with other actions like #toggle_mute that call `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic)`. An explicit `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` is needed before mutating or rendering.

findings.title: unsubscribe toggles notification level instead of unsubscribing, and does not record the change reason
findings.body: The unsubscribe endpoint is linked from notification emails as 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic', but the implementation toggles between `regular` and `muted` depending on the current level: a user at `watching`/`tracking` is set to `regular` (still notified), and a user at `regular` is set to `muted`. So a watching user clicking the email link will keep receiving notifications, and the page text ('You will stop receiving notifications for ...') is false for them. Additionally, the update bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not set and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` event is published, leaving the client UI out of sync. The action should set the level explicitly (muted) via TopicUser.change.

findings.title: unsubscribe is a state-changing GET request
findings.body: The route `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb lines 440-441) makes a mutating operation (changing the user's notification level) reachable via GET. Email clients, link previewers, and crawlers prefetch GET URLs, so merely opening/previewing the unsubscribe link in an email can silently change the user's notification state. This also breaks the `check_xhr` skip semantics and makes the action non-idempotent from a crawler's perspective. The state change should be a POST/PUT (with the GET page rendering the confirmation UI), or at minimum the mutation should require an explicit confirmation.

findings.title: check_xhr is skipped for unsubscribe, allowing non-XHR state changes
findings.body: `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` disables the CSRF/XHR check for the unsubscribe action. Combined with the GET route, this means the notification-level mutation can be triggered by any cross-site GET request (e.g., an tag on a third-party page pointing at the unsubscribe URL) while the victim is logged in, since no CSRF token is required for GET. This is a CSRF risk on a state-changing endpoint.

findings.title: Route creates a new topic record with only an id, producing an invalid/partial model
findings.body: The model hook does `this.store.createRecord("topic", { id: params.id })` and then `topic.updateFromJson(json)`. createRecord pushes a brand-new (unsaved, empty) record into the Ember Data store; updateFromJson then mutates it. This leaves a phantom 'new' topic record in the store (isNew remains true, and it is not properly materialized as a loaded record), which can confuse other code that queries the store for topic id, and the record lacks the slug needed by the template/controller (stopNotificiationsText uses model.fancyTitle, which will be undefined). The correct pattern is `this.store.find('topic', params.id)` or pushing the JSON via store.pushPayload, not createRecord.

findings.title: PostStream.loadTopicView is not a known API and the route ignores slug/access errors
findings.body: `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` is called without any evidence this static method exists on the PostStream model in this codebase (the model exposes instance methods like refresh; topic loading normally goes through the store or Discourse.Topic). If it does not exist, the route's model hook throws and the unsubscribe page fails to load. Additionally, the promise rejection is unhandled, so a 404/403 for a topic the user cannot see results in an unhandled error rather than a proper error page.

findings.title: Typo in property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing the 'a' in 'Notifications'), and the template references `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` so it works, but the misspelling will confuse future maintainers and any external references. It should be renamed to `stopNotificationsText` in both the controller and the template.

findings.title: Triple-stache rendering of stopNotificiationsText injects the topic title as raw HTML
findings.body: The template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (unescaped). The string is built from `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`. `fancyTitle` is HTML-escaped server-side (ERB::Util.html_escape in Topic#fancy_title), but I18n interpolation does not re-escape interpolated values, and the locale string itself wraps {{title}} in <strong> tags. If fancyTitle ever contains markup that survives escaping (e.g., via SmartyPants entities or a title containing encoded entities that get double-unescaped), or if the translation is overridden, this becomes an HTML injection vector in the unsubscribe page. The title should be passed through Ember's escaping (double-stache with a separate escaped binding) rather than triple-stache of a pre-interpolated string.

findings.title: dropdown-button renderString interpolates unescaped values into HTML (XSS)
findings.body:
renderString builds HTML by string concatenation: `buffer.push("
  • ")` and `buffer.push("" + row.title + "")` etc. None of `id`, `row.title`, `row.description`, `row.styleClasses`, `this.get('text')`, `title`, or `longDescription` are HTML-escaped. Any caller that passes user-controlled data (topic titles, category names, usernames) into these fields gets HTML/XSS injection in the dropdown. The change in this PR (adding the `title` field) expands the attack surface. All interpolated values should be escaped (e.g., with a Handlebars escape or _.escape) before being pushed into the buffer.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url passed to email template args is never used by the text body path consistently
findings.body: `send_notification_email` now passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` into email_opts, which flows into template_args. The HTML path substitutes it via the `%{unsubscribe_link}` placeholder in the locale string, but the plain-text body path in Email::MessageBuilder#body appends `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` — this works only because template_args includes unsubscribe_url. However, other callers of build_email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (e.g., the digest mailer, which sets its own @unsubscribe_key and does not pass unsubscribe_url) will now render the new locale text with a missing `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, producing a broken link ('... [click here]().') or an I18n missing-interpolation error in digest emails. The digest path (UserNotifications#digest) must also supply an unsubscribe_url or the locale must be split.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header still points only to user preferences, not the per-topic unsubscribe URL
findings.body: header_args sets `result['List-Unsubscribe'] = "<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>"` when add_unsubscribe_link is set. Now that a per-topic `unsubscribe_url` is available in template_args (passed by UserNotifications#send_notification_email), the List-Unsubscribe header — the one-click unsubscribe mechanism used by Gmail and other mail clients — still directs users to the generic preferences page instead of the topic-specific unsubscribe URL. For one-click unsubscribe to actually stop notifications for the topic (and to satisfy RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe semantics for this feature), the header should use `template_args[:unsubscribe_url]` when present, falling back to user_preferences_url.

findings.title: Unsubscribe link placeholder only substituted in html_override path; plain-text emails rely on body method
findings.body:
The template now includes `
%{unsubscribe_link}
`, which is only substituted in MessageBuilder#html_part (via html_override.gsub!). For notification emails that use the template-based text body (no html_override), the `%{unsubscribe_link}` placeholder is appended by MessageBuilder#body, so the HTML template change is consistent for the html_override path. However, the template is also rendered directly in UserNotifications#send_notification_email via UserNotificationRenderer for the non-template-HTML path — in that path the `%{unsubscribe_link}` and `%{respond_instructions}` placeholders are NOT substituted before being passed as html_override... actually they are substituted later by html_part's gsub!, so this is fine; but note the renderer output is passed as html_override and gsub! mutates it in place, which is acceptable. No concrete defect beyond the digest-path gap noted separately; flagging only that the placeholder substitution depends on add_unsubscribe_link being set, and any email using this template without that flag will leak the literal '%{unsubscribe_link}' text into the HTML.

findings.title: Route ordering change for moderator-liked/summary may shadow or alter existing URL matching
findings.body: The diff reorders routes: `t/:slug/:topic_id/moderator-liked` was moved after `t/:topic_id/wordpress`, and the `summary` routes had their constraints changed from `{topic_id: /\d+/, post_number: /\d+/}` to `{topic_id: /\d+/}`. The constraint change for `t/:slug/:topic_id/summary` and `t/:topic_id/summary` removes the post_number constraint that was previously (incorrectly) present, which is fine, but the reordering means `t/:topic_id/wordpress` is now matched before `t/:slug/:topic_id/moderator-liked`; since the wordpress route only matches a two-segment path (`t/:topic_id/wordpress`), a URL like `/t/some-slug/123/moderator-liked` has three segments and will not be captured by it, so behavior is preserved. However, the new `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route placed before `t/:topic_id/summary` is fine, but `t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` placed before `put "t/:slug/:topic_id"` is fine for GET. The main risk: `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` (line 441) will also match `/t/123/unsubscribe` where 123 could be a slug-less id — intended. No concrete breakage found, but the reordering was unnecessary churn that increases review risk; the summary constraint change should be verified against existing tests.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url uses absolute url (includes base_url) while other URL helpers use relative or base_uri
findings.body: `unsubscribe_url` is defined as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` where `url` is `self.class.url id, slug, post_number` = `"#{Discourse.base_url}/t/#{slug}/#{id}"` — an absolute URL including the host. This is used in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` for `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url` (fine for redirects) and in `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` as `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` for the email link (fine, emails need absolute URLs). However, the Ember route path is `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` and the controller redirects to `unsubscribe_url` when the slug is missing — the absolute URL works. The inconsistency: `relative_url` uses `Discourse.base_uri` while `url` uses `Discourse.base_url`; if base_uri differs from base_url (e.g., behind a proxy with a different path prefix), unsubscribe_url built from `url` may be wrong for redirects. Minor, but the method should be consistent with how it's consumed.

findings.title: No test verifies the per-topic unsubscribe_url appears in the email body or List-Unsubscribe header
findings.body: The spec adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the message_with_unsubscribe builder, but the existing assertions only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body matches the user_preferences_url. There is no assertion that the body contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL (via the updated `unsubscribe_link` locale string with `%{unsubscribe_url}`), and no assertion that the List-Unsubscribe header uses the topic URL. Without these, the core feature of this PR (per-topic unsubscribe link in emails) is untested; a regression that drops unsubscribe_url from template_args or breaks the locale interpolation would pass CI.

findings.title: Read-modify-write of TopicUser notification_level is not atomic
findings.body: `tu.notification_level` is read, then conditionally assigned, then `tu.save!` — a classic read-modify-write race. Two concurrent requests (e.g., the user clicking the email link while also changing notification state in the UI via set_notifications) can interleave, and the last writer wins, potentially clobbering a `watching` level set by the other request. `TopicUser.change` exists precisely to do an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE and should be used instead of find_by + save!.

findings.title: topicUnsubscribe route is registered as a top-level route, not nested under the topic resource
findings.body: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is declared outside the `this.resource('topic', ...)` block, so the route is named `topicUnsubscribe` rather than `topic.unsubscribe`, and it will not receive the parent `topic` route's model (the route's own model hook must re-fetch the topic, which it attempts via PostStream.loadTopicView). This means the topic is loaded twice (once by the parent resource if it were nested, once here) and the controller hierarchy differs from other topic sub-pages. It should be nested inside the topic resource as `this.route('unsubscribe', { path: '/unsubscribe' })` so it inherits the topic model and matches the server-side URL structure.
